questions.stem: Which constitutional amendment added the words 'Socialist' and 'Secular' to the Preamble of the Indian Constitution?
questions.explanation: The **42nd Constitutional Amendment (1976)** modified the Preamble to add 'Socialist', 'Secular', and changed 'Unity of the Nation' to 'Unity and Integrity of the Nation'. It also added Fundamental Duties (Part IVA) and Article 39A.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The 61st Constitutional Amendment (1988) reduced the minimum voting age for Lok Sabha elections from 21 years to:
questions.explanation: The **61st Amendment (1988)** amended Article 326 to lower the voting age from 21 to **18 years** for elections to the House of the People and State Legislative Assemblies, enabling youth participation in democracy.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Which constitutional amendment inserted Article 21A, providing for the right of children aged 6–14 years to free and compulsory education?
questions.explanation: The **86th Constitutional Amendment (2002)** inserted Article 21A (Right to Education as a Fundamental Right), amended Article 45 (DPSP — early childhood care), and amended Article 51A (Fundamental Duty of parents to provide education). The RTE Act 2009 operationalized it.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The 101st Constitutional Amendment (2016) relates to which major economic reform?
questions.explanation: The **101st Amendment (2016)** introduced the **Goods and Services Tax (GST)**, amending Articles 246A, 269A, 279A, inserting clauses on concurrent power of Parliament and States to legislate on GST, and establishing the GST Council.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Which constitutional amendment introduced the Anti-Defection Law by adding the Tenth Schedule to the Constitution?
questions.explanation: The **52nd Constitutional Amendment (1985)** added the **Tenth Schedule** ('Anti-Defection Law') to the Constitution, providing for disqualification of members of Parliament/State legislatures on grounds of defection from their political parties.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The 73rd Constitutional Amendment (1992) provided constitutional recognition to:
questions.explanation: The **73rd Amendment (1992)** added Part IX and the Eleventh Schedule to the Constitution, giving constitutional status to **Panchayati Raj Institutions**. It mandates elections, reservation of seats (SC/ST/Women), and a three-tier structure in rural areas.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Under which article of the Indian Constitution can Parliament amend any provision of the Constitution?
questions.explanation: **Article 368** deals with 'Power of Parliament to amend the Constitution and procedure therefor'. It lays down three methods: (i) by simple majority, (ii) by special majority (2/3 + absolute majority), and (iii) special majority + ratification by half of State Legislatures.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The 44th Constitutional Amendment (1978) removed the Right to Property from the Fundamental Rights chapter and made it:
options: A Directive Principle of State Policy
A constitutional right under Article 300A (legal right, not fundamental right)
questions.explanation: The **44th Amendment (1978)** deleted Article 19(1)(f) and Article 31 from Part III and inserted **Article 300A** (right to property is a constitutional/legal right). It can now be abridged by law, unlike a fundamental right. This amendment also restored the SC's power of judicial review diluted by the 42nd Amendment.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The 1st Constitutional Amendment (1951) is chiefly remembered for:
options: Adding the Ninth Schedule to protect land reform laws from being struck down under Fundamental Rights
Reducing the voting age from 21 to 18
questions.explanation: The **1st Amendment (1951)** inserted the **Ninth Schedule** to the Constitution, placing land reform laws beyond the reach of judicial review for violating Fundamental Rights (especially Articles 14 and 19). It also validated zamindari abolition acts. The SC later held that post-1973 additions to the Ninth Schedule can be reviewed for basic structure violations.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Which of the following was NOT brought about by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment (1976)?
options: Reduction of voting age from 21 to 18 years
Addition of 'Socialist' and 'Secular' to the Preamble
Extension of Lok Sabha and State Assembly terms from 5 to 6 years
questions.explanation: The **61st Amendment (1988)** reduced the voting age from 21 to 18, NOT the 42nd. The 42nd Amendment (1976) added Fundamental Duties, modified the Preamble, extended Parliament term to 6 years (later reversed by the 44th Amendment), curtailed judicial review, and added DPSP Article 39A.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The 91st Constitutional Amendment (2003) restricts the size of the Council of Ministers (including the Prime Minister) to a maximum of what percentage of the total membership of the Lok Sabha?
questions.explanation: The **91st Amendment (2003)** inserted Article 75(1A), limiting the total number of ministers including the PM to **not more than 15% of the total strength of the Lok Sabha** (i.e., ≤ 81 ministers at present strength of 543). A similar cap applies to State Councils of Ministers.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The 99th Constitutional Amendment (2014) sought to establish which body, which was subsequently struck down by the Supreme Court in 2015?
options: National Right to Free Legal Aid Commission
questions.explanation: The **99th Amendment (2014)** established the **National Judicial Appointments Commission (NJAC)** to replace the collegium system for appointing judges. In October 2015, the Supreme Court (4:1 majority) struck it down as unconstitutional, holding it violated the independence of the judiciary (basic structure).
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The 24th Constitutional Amendment (1971) was enacted primarily to:
options: Affirm Parliament's power to amend any part of the Constitution, including Fundamental Rights
Remove the right to property from Fundamental Rights
questions.explanation: After the Supreme Court's ruling in Golaknath v. State of Punjab (1967) that Parliament cannot abridge Fundamental Rights, the **24th Amendment (1971)** overruled it by inserting Article 13(4) and amending Article 368, asserting that Parliament's constituent power extends to amending all provisions including Fundamental Rights.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The 74th Constitutional Amendment (1992) provided constitutional status to:
questions.explanation: The **74th Amendment (1992)** added Part IXA and the Twelfth Schedule, giving constitutional status to **urban local bodies (municipalities)**. It mandates regular elections, reservation for SC/ST/women, establishment of Ward Committees, and State Finance Commissions for urban areas.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The 103rd Constitutional Amendment (2019) provides for reservation of up to 10% for which group?
options: Other Backward Classes (OBC) in addition to existing quota
Scheduled Castes and Tribes in private sector
Economically Weaker Sections (EWS) among the general category
questions.explanation: The **103rd Amendment (2019)** inserted Articles 15(6) and 16(6), enabling up to **10% reservation for Economically Weaker Sections (EWS)** of citizens NOT covered by existing SC/ST/OBC reservations. Income criteria apply (family income < ₹8 lakh per annum).
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The 7th Constitutional Amendment (1956) is primarily associated with:
options: Reorganization of States on linguistic lines and abolition of Part A/B/C/D state classification
questions.explanation: The **7th Amendment (1956)** implemented the States Reorganisation Act, 1956. It abolished the four-class system (Part A, B, C, D States) and reorganized States on **linguistic lines** following the recommendations of the States Reorganisation Commission (Fazl Ali Commission).
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The 100th Constitutional Amendment (2015) relates to:
options: Exchange of territories with Bangladesh under the Land Boundary Agreement
Giving constitutional status to the NCBC
questions.explanation: The **100th Amendment (2015)** implemented the 1974 Land Boundary Agreement (LBA) between India and Bangladesh (as updated by the 2011 Protocol), facilitating exchange of enclaves — 111 Indian enclaves (17,160 acres) in Bangladesh and 51 Bangladeshi enclaves (7,110 acres) in India.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The 86th Constitutional Amendment (2002) inserted which article to make education a Fundamental Right?
questions.explanation: The 86th Amendment inserted **Article 21A**, which states: 'The State shall provide free and compulsory education to all children of the age of six to fourteen years in such manner as the State may, by law, determine.' Article 45 (DPSP for early childhood care) was also amended.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Under the original anti-defection law (52nd Amendment, 1985), a 'merger' of a political party was recognised only if at least what fraction of its legislature party joined the merger?
questions.explanation: Under the original Tenth Schedule (52nd Amendment), a merger was valid if **at least two-thirds** of a legislature party's members agreed to the merger. The 91st Amendment (2003) removed the 'split' provision (which had been one-third) while retaining the two-thirds merger provision.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The 102nd Constitutional Amendment (2018) gave constitutional status to which body?
questions.explanation: The **102nd Amendment (2018)** inserted Articles 338B and 342A, giving constitutional status to the **National Commission for Backward Classes (NCBC)**. Article 342A empowers the President (with concurrence of States for State lists) to specify socially and educationally backward classes.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Which constitutional amendment abolished the provision for nominated seats for Anglo-Indians in the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies?
questions.explanation: The **104th Amendment (2020)** extended reservation for SC/ST in the Lok Sabha and State Assemblies for another 10 years (till 2030) and **abolished the provision for nominated Anglo-Indian seats** in Parliament and State Legislatures, ending a colonial-era provision (original Articles 331 and 333).
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The 'basic structure' doctrine was first applied to actually invalidate a specific constitutional amendment (not just proclaimed) in which case?
options: Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala (1973)
Minerva Mills v. Union of India (1980)
Waman Rao v. Union of India (1981)
questions.explanation: While the basic structure doctrine was **proclaimed** in Kesavananda Bharati (1973), it was **first applied to strike down provisions of a constitutional amendment** in **Minerva Mills (1980)**, which invalidated Sections 4 and 55 of the 42nd Amendment that had curtailed judicial review and Parliamentary amendments beyond challenge.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The Ninth Schedule was added to the Constitution by the 1st Amendment (1951). What is its primary purpose?
options: Lists laws on cooperative societies protected from review
Lists laws related to property rights protected from challenge
Lists land reform and state regulation laws protected from challenge under Fundamental Rights provisions
Lists laws on linguistic minority protections
questions.explanation: The **Ninth Schedule** (added by the 1st Amendment, 1951) contains laws — primarily related to **land reforms, agrarian legislation, and State regulation of trade** — that are shielded from challenge under Fundamental Rights (Articles 13, 14, 19, 31). Laws added after April 24, 1973 can still be reviewed for basic structure violations (I.R. Coelho case, 2007).
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Under Article 368, which type of amendments requires ratification by at least half of the State Legislatures in addition to a special majority in Parliament?
options: Amendments affecting federal structure — e.g., election of President, distribution of legislative powers, representation of States in Parliament, Article 368 itself
questions.explanation: Under Article 368(2), certain federal provisions require **special majority + ratification by not less than half of State Legislatures**: election of President, extent of executive power of Union/States, distribution of legislative powers (Lists), Supreme/High Court provisions, representation of States in Parliament, and Article 368 itself. Other amendments need only a special majority.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The Supreme Court's ruling in the I.R. Coelho v. State of Tamil Nadu (2007) case (9-judge bench) held that regarding the Ninth Schedule:
options: All Ninth Schedule laws are permanently beyond judicial review
Only criminal laws in the Ninth Schedule can be challenged
Laws inserted into the Ninth Schedule after April 24, 1973 (date of Kesavananda Bharati judgment) can be challenged if they violate the basic structure of the Constitution
The Ninth Schedule can be amended only by a unanimous vote of Parliament
questions.explanation: In **I.R. Coelho (2007)**, the SC (9-judge bench) held that laws placed in the Ninth Schedule **after April 24, 1973** (the date of the Kesavananda Bharati ruling) are NOT immune from judicial review if they damage or destroy the basic structure of the Constitution. Laws added before that date retain full immunity.
questions.subject: Polity
